steps.description:
The diagram belows shows a region bounded by left and right limits.\

Write a program that performs the following: 1. Ask user to input coordinates of a point x,y. 2. Ask user to input the region boundaries (min and max x-coordinates) separated by space. 3.Call a function to check if the point falls within the region (including the boundaries). It will then display the returned result.

You will need to write a function that takes in the point coordinates and region boundaries (min and max x-coordinates). It will return True if the point falls within the region or False if otherwise.

Follow the test output display format and comment your codes.

Test Input 2.1,0 -2 2

-10.1,5 -10 0

2,0 -2 2

-10,5 -10 -9

Test Output (Red Text - User Input) Test your program with the examples below: Example 1 Enter point (x,y): 2.1,0 Enter min x and max x: -2 2 False

Example 2 Enter point (x,y): -10.1,5 Enter min x and max x: -10 0 False

Example 3 Enter point (x,y): 2,0 Enter min x and max x: -2 2 True

Example 4 Enter point (x,y): -10,5 Enter min x and max x: -10 -9 True

The diagram belows shows a region bounded by top and bottom limits.


Write a program that performs the following: 1. Ask user to input coordinates of a point x,y. 2. Ask user to input the region boundaries (min and max y-coordinates) separated by space. 3.Call a function to check if the point falls within the region (including the boundaries). It will then display the returned result.

You will need to write a function that takes in the point coordinates and region boundaries (min and max y-coordinates). It will return True if the point falls within the region or False if otherwise.

Follow the test output display format and comment your codes.

Test Input 0,2.1 -2 2

1,-10.1 -10 0

2,2 -2 2

-10,-9 -10 -9

Test Output (Red Text - User Input) Test your program with the examples below:

Example 1 Enter point (x,y): 0,2.1 Enter min y and max y: -2 2 False

Example 2 Enter point (x,y): 1,-10.1 Enter min y and max y: -10 0 False

Example 3 Enter point (x,y): 2,2 Enter min y and max y: -2 2 True

Example 4 Enter point (x,y): -10,-9 Enter min y and max y: -10 -9 True

Collision detection is an important function in many applications such as games, simulations, animation, etc. In this exercise, you will practise writing a simple algorithm for detecting the collision of a point and a rectangle.

You wanted to check if a cannon ball fired by a cannon has hit a castle at a certain point of time. The cannon ball's position is presented by point coordinates while the castle's boundaries are represented by a rectangle. Below shows a sample illustration.

Create a program that performs the following 1. Ask user to input the coordinates of the cannonball in the format x,y. 2. Ask user to input the 4 corners of a rectangle representing the castle boundaries in the format x1,y1 x2,y2 x3,y3 x4,y4. Note that the points may not be in any order. 3. Call a function to check for collision return "hit" if it collided or "not hit" if otherwise. 4. Display the returned result.

You will need to create a function that takes in the coordinates of the cannonball and the castle's boundaries. The function will return True if the cannonball is either touching or inside the rectangle. Otherwise, it will return False. You may add more functions.

Follow the test output display format and comment your codes.

Test Input 2,2 0,6 5,6 5,0 0,0

0,0 5,6 5,0 0,6 0,0

5,6 0,0 0,6 5,6 5,0

4,0 0,0 5,6 0,6 5,0

-5,-5 9,9 9,-9 -9,9 -9,-9

-10,11 -9,9 9,9 9,-9 -9,-9

12,0 9,-9 -9,-9 -9,9 9,9

Test Output (Red Text - User Input) Test your program with the examples below:

Example 1 Enter coordinate of cannon ball: 2,2 Enter boundary of castle: 0,6 5,6 5,0 0,0 hit

Example 2 Enter coordinate of cannon ball: 0,0 Enter boundary of castle: 5,6 5,0 0,6 0,0 hit

Example 3 Enter coordinate of cannon ball: 5,6 Enter boundary of castle: 0,0 0,6 5,6 5,0 hit

Example 4
Enter coordinate of cannon ball: 4,0
Enter boundary of castle: 0,0 5,6 0,6 5,0 hit

Example 5
Enter coordinate of cannon ball: -5,-5 Enter boundary of castle: 9,9 9,-9 -9,9 -9,-9 hit

Example 6 Enter coordinate of cannon ball: -10,11 Enter boundary of castle: -9,9 9,9 9,-9 -9,-9 not hit Example 7 Enter coordinate of cannon ball: 12,0 Enter boundary of castle: 9,-9 -9,-9 -9,9 9,9 not hit

The castle has been upgraded with a tower. The new castle boundaries can be represented by 2 rectangles as shown below.


Create a program that performs the following 1. Ask user to input the coordinates of the cannonball in the format x,y. 2. Ask user to input the 4 corners of a rectangle 1, representing the castle boundaries in the format x1,y1 x2,y2 x3,y3 x4,y4. Note that the points may not be in any order. 3. Ask user to input the 4 corners of a rectangle 2, representing the tower boundaries in the format x1,y1 x2,y2 x3,y3 x4,y4. Note that the points may not be in any order. 3. Call a function to check for collision and display "hit" if the function returns True. Otherwise, display "not hit".

You will need to create a function that takes in the coordinates of the cannonball and the boundaries. The function will return True if the cannonball is either touching or inside the boundaries. Otherwise, it will return False. You may add more functions.

Follow the test output display format and comment your codes.

Test Input -5.1,4 -5,0 5,0 5,4 -5,4 0,4 3,10, 3,4 0,10

-0.1, 4.1 -5,0 5,0 5,4 -5,4 0,4 3,4 0,10 3,10

3,10.1 5,4 -5,4 -5,0 5,0 0,10 0,4 3,10 3,4

3.1,4.1 -5,0 5,0 -5,4 5,4 0,4 3,4 0,10 3,10

-5,-0.1 -5,0 5,0 5,4 -5,4 0,4 0,10 3,10 3,4

-5,4 -5,0 -5,4 5,0 5,4 0,4 3,10 3,4 0,10

3,3.9 -5,0 5,0 -5,4 5,4 0,4 3,10 3,4 0,10

5,0.1 -5,0 5,0 5,4 -5,4 0,10 0,4 3,10 3,4

Test Output (Red Text - User Input) Test your program with the examples below: Example 1

Enter coordinate of cannon ball: -5.1,4 Enter boundary of castle: -5,0 5,0 5,4 -5,4 Enter boundary of tower: 0,4 3,10, 3,4 0,10 not hit

Example 2 Enter coordinate of cannon ball: -0.1, 4.1 Enter boundary of castle: -5,0 5,0 5,4 -5,4 Enter boundary of tower: 0,4 3,4 0,10 3,10 not hit

Example 3
Enter coordinate of cannon ball: 3,10.1 Enter boundary of castle: 5,4 -5,4 -5,0 5,0 Enter boundary of tower: 0,10 0,4 3,10 3,4 not hit
Example 4 Enter coordinate of cannon ball: 3.1,4.1 Enter boundary of castle: -5,0 5,0 -5,4 5,4 Enter boundary of tower: 0,4 3,4 0,10 3,10 not hit Example 5 Enter coordinate of cannon ball: -5,-0.1 Enter boundary of castle: -5,0 5,0 5,4 -5,4 Enter boundary of tower: 0,4 0,10 3,10 3,4 not hit Example 6 Enter coordinate of cannon ball: -5,4 Enter boundary of castle: -5,0 -5,4 5,0 5,4 Enter boundary of tower: 0,4 3,10 3,4 0,10 hit
Example 7 Enter coordinate of cannon ball: 3,3.9 Enter boundary of castle: -5,0 5,0 -5,4 5,4 Enter boundary of tower: 0,4 3,10 3,4 0,10 hit Example 8 Enter coordinate of cannon ball: 5,0.1 Enter boundary of castle: -5,0 5,0 5,4 -5,4 Enter boundary of tower: 0,10 0,4 3,10 3,4 hit
